source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The client checks whether its processed data buffer is greater than 16 MiB. It first allocates and copies a combined partial buffer when needed, and events received while processing are queued before that check. The change is therefore not a hard peak-allocation or total-queue memory cap. Exactly 16 MiB is allowed by the comparison. No boundary, memory-pressure or LDAP execution was performed.
title: The LDAP receive cap runs after concatenation and does not cap queued or peak memory
